note: Mat4 and the units it carries. Run 2026-09-20: twelve mutants, eleven caught, one declared survivor, none invalid. Three of these are the row/column-major transpositions the file exists to prevent, and one -- the rigid inverse computing -R t instead of -R^T t -- is not hypothetical: it is the defect this task actually shipped into the working tree and the round-trip test caught, 1.9 m out at a scale of 1 m. Six of the eleven die at compile time, which is the most any pass in this project has had. Two kills are for a different reason than their name suggests, and HISTORY.md says which.

mutants.name: the rigid inverse turns the translation by R instead of R transposed
mutants.replace:
result.at(12 + row) =
            -((e.at(row) * e.at(12)) + (e.at(4 + row) * e.at(13)) + (e.at(8 + row) * e.at(14)));

mutants.name: the rigid inverse does not negate the translation
the rigid inverse copies the rotation block instead of transposing it
multiplication reads the left operand transposed
multiplication reads the right operand transposed
transpose copies instead of transposing
transformPoint drops the translation
mutants.find:
out.at(row) = (e.at(row) * p.x.value()) + (e.at(4 + row) * p.y.value()) +
                      (e.at(8 + row) * p.z.value()) + e.at(12 + row);
mutants.replace:
out.at(row) = (e.at(row) * p.x.value()) + (e.at(4 + row) * p.y.value()) +
                      (e.at(8 + row) * p.z.value());

mutants.name: transformDirection applies the translation
mutants.find:
out.at(row) = (e.at(row) * d.x.value()) + (e.at(4 + row) * d.y.value()) +
                      (e.at(8 + row) * d.z.value());
mutants.replace:
out.at(row) = (e.at(row) * d.x.value()) + (e.at(4 + row) * d.y.value()) +
                      (e.at(8 + row) * d.z.value()) + e.at(12 + row);

mutants.name: a translation writes its components into the wrong row
mutants.find:
m.set(Row{0}, Column{3}, t.x.value());
    m.set(Row{1}, Column{3}, t.y.value());
mutants.replace:
m.set(Row{0}, Column{3}, t.y.value());
    m.set(Row{1}, Column{3}, t.x.value());

mutants.name: isAffine accepts anything
mutants.find:
return bitsOf(e.at(3)) == bitsOf(0.0) && bitsOf(e.at(7)) == bitsOf(0.0) &&
           bitsOf(e.at(11)) == bitsOf(0.0) && bitsOf(e.at(15)) == bitsOf(1.0);

mutants.name: the perspective divide multiplies by w
mutants.find:
p.xyz.x.value() / p.w.value(),
        p.xyz.y.value() / p.w.value(),
        p.xyz.z.value() / p.w.value(),
mutants.replace:
p.xyz.x.value() * p.w.value(),
        p.xyz.y.value() * p.w.value(),
        p.xyz.z.value() * p.w.value(),
mutants.why: Nothing in M1-09 evaluates the divide numerically: its only assertion about perspectiveDivide is the static_assert on the reference it returns, which a sign or an operator does not change. The numerical claim belongs to M1-10, whose near-plane test reads depth through this function -- so this mutant is declared surviving here and is expected to be caught there. Recorded rather than closed by a test invented for it (VERIFICATION.md rule 19).
